newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 14.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 14.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Friday:
* On Thursday, the Dow Jones climbed 60.81 points to 7,022.44. PLDT's ADR dropped $0 7/8 to $61 1/8.
* The peso closed up at 26.343 to a U.S. dollar from 26.347.
* The Philippine Stock Exchange composite index shed 4.10 points to 3,335.73.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was unchanged at 10.53125 percent.
*Music Semiconductor Corp is expected to post a net income of 244.9 million pesos in 1997, president Steve Stas told an investors briefing on Thursday.
Stas said Music's revenues are expected to rise to 817.6 million pesos in 1997.
Earlier on Thursday, Music Semiconductor told the Philippine Stock Exchange its net income soared by 155 percent to 160.214 million pesos in 1996 from 62.752 million in 1995.
It also said revenues in 1996 reached 510.008 million pesos from 311.431 million in the previous year.
*Philippine conglomerate Metro Pacific Corp said on Thursday it posted a 64 percent rise in net profit in 1996 to 843.9 million pesos as its diversification efforts began to show a return.
The company, a unit of Hong Kong's First Pacific Co Ltd, said in a statement that equity in net earnings of affiliated companies grew 207 percent in the year to 485.5 million pesos.
*The Philippine Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) said on Thursday it had summoned officials of five listed companies to explain a surge in their stock prices since the start of the year.
SEC chairman Perfecto Yasay told reporters show-cause notices had been sent to Itogon-Suyoc Mines Inc, Atok Big Wedge Co Inc, Pacifica Inc, Acoje Holdings Inc and Marsteel Consolidated Inc.
*Packaging firm Steniel Manufacturing Corp on Thursday reported a net loss of 245.6 million pesos in 1996.

*Manila Electric Co, the country's biggest electricity distributor, posted an unaudited net income of 5.0 billion pesos in 1996 compared with the previous year's 4.4 billion, First Philippine Holdings Corp said on Thursday in its quarterly interim report.
FPHC is the biggest shareholder of Meralco.

*Philippine Telegraph & Telephone Corp reported on Thursday a lower net loss of 26 million pesos in the first half of its its fiscal year 1996/97 compared with 42 million pesos in the same period last year.
The company's fiscal year starts on July 1.
